session.title: rn that achieves a purpose from a request alone

goals.what: Whoever wants to hand a whole piece of work to an agent asks for it without preparing anything, only answers what they are asked, and their purpose is achieved; rn 0.10.0 brings this to them.
goals.why: Work that takes days then reaches a merged result with the user called only for their own decisions, deciding each sign-off from the proposal alone and going on from the record the next day, as issue #54 says.

acceptance_criteria.what: On real requests, the user sends back few changes at the deliverable sign-off, none once G1 is reached.
On the same requests, the user spends little time from asking to their purpose achieved, with AC1 no worse.

tasks.what: lane holds a plugin's flow: the plugin declares the order its roles go in, and lane gives each next move and holds the orchestrator to it

completion_criteria.what: lane's README, UX and architecture promise and design the flow, each passing its template's questions and agreed by the user
lane depends on no plugin: no code, document or example of it names turn, rn or another ccpm plugin
check.sh lane 100%, mutate.sh lane 0 survivors, and its trials passing

tasks.what: Pin, a plugin of its own in ccpm, pins a plan down from its purpose: a design tree from the goal down, the user asked only what is theirs, one point at a time, nothing left assumed; Turn and rn take it in by dependencies

completion_criteria.what: Pin's skill, pin:down, made from Matt Pocock's grilling skill (MIT, credited) and the design tree agreed on 2026-10-31, and its script checking a design-tree.json: every question served, every decision reaching the root, the order following builds_on
tried first: a role of Turn runs the script of Pin, its dependency, and Lane checks that call; if it cannot, where the script lies is decided again
Pin is built by .claude/rules/dev.md: check.sh Pin 100%, mutate.sh Pin 0 survivors, and its trials passing

status.next_step: Where it stands, 2026-11-05: Lane's, Pin's and Turn's UX, README, architecture, code and tests were remade, but the remake drifted from what the user agreed, without asking. Held, to be put to the user when the plugin it touches is rebuilt, each asked whether it is still needed: (1) a go-between relay in Pin and Turn, plugins/pin/core/roles/go-between.md among it (the user decided subagents ask the main conversation directly); (2) Turn's designer removed; (3) the evaluator giving more/met/reword/good instead of good/more, to fit Lane's routing; (4) Lane's every_item and end_when unused while Turn re-checks the same in phases.py; (5) dev/plugin-best-practice.md's Nobody relays rewritten in 8602092c (to revert, keeping its no-prompt-trial part); (6) the Lane commits 281dae86, 1e690d7d, 6c8bfa5e and f16c1cda, kept on the branch lane-held, out of rebuild. Done: each document kind's form is a template beside its best practice, with Turn's own document as its example, made by meta.json, which has its own template, meta-template.json; Turn's one design tree, dev/turn/design-tree.json, holds its UX and README. Next: the user reviews ux (template, example), then readme, then architecture by the same flow, then the remaining kinds, then parts are removed from the form once no kind uses it; then Lane's and Pin's trees. Open for the user: the architecture's scope (architecture.json asks for structure too, not design intent only), and where Turn's orchestrator runs, as Lane checks only subagents. rn is out of scope, held at 0.8.0. Push with git -c core.hooksPath=dev/scripts/githooks push, and read its CI before the next push.
